t: Rome made Carthage's land a province in 146 BCE; Augustus united it with Africa Nova and refounded Carthage as its capital.
Its grain, olive oil and fine pottery fed and furnished Rome, and its cities were among the richest in the empire.
It was a heartland of Latin Christianity, home to Tertullian, Cyprian and the long Donatist schism.
dyk: The Acts of the Scillitan Martyrs, about Christians tried at Carthage in 180, are the oldest dated Christian document written in Latin.
ev: Rome destroys Carthage and creates the province of Africa, governed from Utica
Caesar annexes Numidian lands as Africa Nova after Thapsus
Augustus unites the provinces as Africa Proconsularis, with Carthage as capital
Revolt of Tacfarinas among the peoples of the interior
A revolt at Thysdrus proclaims Gordian I emperor
Diocletian divides the province, creating Byzacena and Tripolitania
The Vandals under Gaiseric seize Carthage
